content.comment_body: How can I adjust the first two values using the plus and minus buttons? What needs to be changed in the program?
I'm not sure I understand your question.
Sorry, I find it hard to explain. I want to change values up and down using the F3 and F4 buttons but don't know how to do it. Is this related to what I mentioned before?
Please upload your entire program as an [document] file so I can assist you better.
It's a network project, so I uploaded the project file. The text is in Swedish.

No offense, but your program layout is quite chaotic. The display won't update because the timer parameter isn't linked to the setpoint adjuster. Even if you create that connection, another issue comes up: the displayed value won't be the actual time value, but the block number it's referencing.

Yeah, the program is really messy; it's my first project and I've just started learning [product_name] programming a few weeks ago. I think I follow what you're saying, but I don't know how to fix it.

You can't simply change how this is shown. If you want to avoid seeing the block number as a reference in the display, the best you can do is show the counter value. But then the value appears as seconds and not in a formatted manner like s: / 100s or m: s. For example, 5 seconds and 40 hundredths will show as 540, not 05:40s. If you select seconds as the time base, 5 minutes and 40 seconds will show as 340 instead of 05:40m.
I don't mind if 5 s and 40 hundredths appear as 540. I just want to be able to adjust the value up and down with F3 and F4. But I'm not sure how to link the timer parameter to the setpoint adjuster.
I've created references for the first two timers and updated the message texts. This should help guide you.
Thank you so much for all the help! If I want a submenu, do I need to make new setpoint adjusters for that?
I'm sorry, I don't understand your question.

I'll try to clarify. If I create another menu page with three more timers, how do I make these timers adjustable? Do I need separate setpoint adjusters for each, or can I add them all to a single adjuster?
Each setpoint requires its own setpoint adjuster.
Okay, that's what I thought.
It seems you don't quite understand how main and submenu structures work together.
Can you explain what you mean?
I wish there were more guides about menus. I've watched some YouTube videos, but couldn't find other resources.

There's another way to adjust timer values or setpoints for other blocks directly through the display. There's a file and a screen video showing how to change values on the display in simulation or in real life using the web server. The steps for changing settings via the [product_name] display are as follows: Sorry, but the files can't be attached right now due to server issues. I'll provide them later. Edit: attaching file.

Can I adjust only the first parameter with F3 + and F4 -? The arrow doesn't move when I press the cursor key down; it stays at the top row. Maybe there's an issue with my program. It's not a big problem; I can use the method you suggested. But using cursor up/down and F3/F4 would be easier.

The simulation works, but it doesn't function on the TDE or the display. It also works from the web interface, where I can move the arrow up and down. Is this a hardware or software problem? Device=FS01, Firmware version=TDE V1.08.01
It's actually a user issue. You're just making an error.
Looks like you were right. If you press ESC and the cursor key down together, the arrow moves. Now everything works! Thanks for all your help.

analysis.insight_summary: Users face challenges configuring their hardware to allow value changes using the F3 and F4 buttons. There is confusion about how to link timer settings with setpoint adjusters, and the device shows block numbers instead of intuitive time values. Users discuss possible workarounds and ways to improve their program structure.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect an easy way to adjust timer values on the device display using F3 and F4 buttons, and clear guidance on linking display parameters to adjustable settings.
